title: Six confident auto-handles of security, lookup and no-issue tweets (6 missed)
hypothesis: All six survivors sit at confidence 0.90-0.98, so the guard cannot touch them, and no lexical rule fires ('broke into' is not in the security regex; 'Check your DMs' and screenshot captions pass min_words). The LLM proposes auto_handle because the retrieved evidence is dominated by self-serve and template replies (all 17 needs_account_lookup histories ask for a DM, but the model drafts steps instead). The pipeline already detects the clash between the LLM's auto_handle and the intent's default_decision: escalate (trace.policy_conflict is True on g_215) but only logs it, so a hacked-account tweet classified correctly at 0.98 still ships with a link. Zero-shot escalated 4 of the 6 (g_042, g_105, g_151, g_215).

examples.text: I think I had someone who broke into my spotify, as another user was on and deleted my playlists and made new ones. Help???
examples.reply_draft: Hey there! We’re sorry to hear that. Check out the help article for what to do next: https://support.spotify.com/article/hacked-account /AI
examples.why: Intent account_hacked_or_security at 0.98 whose default_decision is escalate, yet policy_conflict was logged instead of enforced and the reply pastes a help link from memory.

examples.text: I've got the "Get a year of Premium" offer splash screen on my iOs app, but there wasn't any CTA to apply just a button to open a webpage... and there is no button, link or anything... How can I apply?!?! 🧐🤨 #Spotify #SpotifyPremium
examples.reply_draft: Hey there! Help's here. Can you try heading to this link:? Let us know how it goes 🧐 /AI
examples.why: Every historical reply for this offer asks for a DM, but the agent copied a link template whose URL was scrubbed, leaving 'this link:?'.

examples.reply_draft: Hey there! Help's here. Can you let us know how we can assist? Keep us posted /AI
examples.why: Same miss as v1: three words pass min_words_for_auto_handle and no rule matches 'check your DMs', so the agent asks what the issue is.

proposed_fix: (1) Enforce the default: when trace.policy_conflict is True and the intent's default_decision is escalate (security, billing, login, other), set decision=escalate with the intent's default_reason_code; test: g_215 and g_151 become escalate, no change on rows without conflict. (2) Add rules: security 'broke into|hijack(ed)?|another user (was|is) on'; ambiguous 'check (your|my|the) dms?' and captions of <=8 words ending in <url>; repeated-contact 'how many times'. (3) DM-consistency rule: if >=2 of the top-3 cited brand replies ask for a DM and the LLM says auto_handle, escalate as needs_account_lookup; test on dev that missed escalations drop to <=3 at precision >=0.68.

title: URL scrub leaves dangling 'more info here:' with no link in 33 replies
hypothesis: The v1 fix scrubbed '<url>' and bare home-page links from the evidence shown to the model, but left the clause that introduces them ('Check out the steps ... at <url>', 'Dutch support via email at <url>'). The model copies the template verbatim (its grounding_notes say 'taken directly from evidence thread'), so 33 replies end in 'here: /AI', 'at. Let us know' or 'this link:?'. 30 of these 33 rows carried a placeholder or fake link in v1: the defect moved from a wrong link to a missing one. The judge flagged only 8 as hallucinated (11 non-ship) and shipped 22 with grounded >= 4, so the reported 5% flag rate understates it three-fold. Two further replies (g_215, g_250) contain URLs present in no evidence entry, and two (g_127, g_217) promise that developers are 'looking into this'.

examples.text: if you really cared, you'd fix your Roku app. Not being able to access my playlists is really getting in the way of my Xmas spirit.
examples.reply_draft: Hey there! We have some info about the Spotify app on Roku here:. Give us a shout if there's anything else 🙂 /AI
examples.why: The cited brand reply is 'info about the Spotify app on Roku here: <url>'; the scrub removed the URL and the agent kept 'here:.' verbatim.

examples.text: Hi guys, my downloaded songs keep getting unrecognized when I go offline. I have to keep selecting "download" and it is frustrating when I want to listen to music on a plane not having offline content. Why is this happening on my LGV10 Android?
examples.reply_draft: Hey! Sorry to hear that. Check out the steps under “Downloads unexpectedly removed” at. Let us know how it goes 💚 /AI
examples.why: The 'Downloads unexpectedly removed' template is topically right, but 'at.' points nowhere; the judge rejected it with grounded 1.

examples.reply_draft: Hey there! We're launching in new countries as often as possible. Be sure to add your email at /AI
examples.why: Tells the customer to add their email 'at' nothing; the historical reply linked a launch-notification page that was scrubbed.

proposed_fix: Scrub the referring clause, not just the token: when removing <url> from an evidence reply, also delete the trailing 'here:|at|over at|via email at|link:' fragment, or substitute a canonical link from a small map (downloads-removed -> support.spotify.com/article/listen-offline, community ideas -> community.spotify.com/t5/Ideas). Add a post-generation validator that rejects a draft matching r'(here|at|link)\s*:?\s*[.?]?\s*(emoji)?\s*/AI$' and re-prompts once. Test: zero replies match the pattern on the 200 test rows; judge hallucination flags on these 33 rows drop from 8 to 0; every URL in a reply must appear in evidence.resolved_links or the canonical map.

title: 'other' captions and chit-chat take the nearest thread's intent: 14 errors
hypothesis: BM25 matches the caption's nouns (Switzerland, names, Modest Mouse, presale, playlists) to a thread with a real issue and the classifier adopts that thread's intent: 8 became feature_request_or_feedback, 4 subscription_or_plan. Six of the 14 are screenshot captions ending in <url>, five are chit-chat or venting, two are presale codes, one a job request. Zero-shot shared 7 of the 14 and got 5 right, so roughly half is retrieval-induced and half a prompt gap (the prompt never says a tweet that points at an attached image is 'other'). 10 of 14 are gold escalate; 7 were rescued only by the 0.9 guard (recorded as low_confidence, which is why 11 of 21 ambiguous_or_media_only rows carry the wrong reason code) and 3 were missed outright (g_042, g_088, g_211).

examples.text: . Any ETA on solving this issue?: <url>
examples.reply_draft: Hey! We're afraid we don't have any info to share, but rest assured we’re working on it as we speak. Stay tuned 🙂 /AI
examples.why: A caption for a screenshot ('this issue') retrieved a Discover Weekly thread; the agent invented a feature-feedback intent and a status update at 0.9.

examples.text: How do I fix this? They all have different names. <url>
examples.reply_draft: Hey there! Can you send over the URIs of the contents that should be on a separate page? Just right-click the track > Share > URI /AI
examples.why: 'They all have different names. <url>' matched an artist-profile thread, so the agent asked for track URIs about a problem only visible in the image.

examples.text: how many times do I have to tell you that I hate Modest Mouse
examples.reply_draft: Hey there! We hear you, and we'll be sure to pass your feedback on to the right folks. Let us know how it goes 🙂 /AI
examples.why: A vent with no request retrieved a feedback thread; the agent promised to pass feedback on instead of asking what is wrong.

proposed_fix: Add to the system prompt: 'If the tweet refers to something not in the text (this, that, the screenshot, ends in <url> with under ~10 words) or contains no request, label other and escalate ambiguous_or_media_only.' Add a deterministic caption rule: text ending in <url> with <=8 other words and no issue keyword -> other/ambiguous. Test on dev: 'other' recall >= 0.75 with no drop in other classes' F1; the ambiguous_or_media_only -> low_confidence confusion count falls from 11 to <=3.

title: 0.9 confidence guard escalates 28 correct auto-handles, 24 of them at 0.85
hypothesis: Confidence is a 5-value ordinal (0.85/0.9/0.95/0.99 cover 162 of 200 rows) and 0.85 means 'topic recognised, tweet vague or venting', not 'intent uncertain': intent accuracy is 0.57 in the 0.80-0.89 bin. Of 36 unnecessary escalations 28 are threshold-induced (7 LLM-chosen needs_account_lookup, 1 rule-forced on '$99'). The sweep shows the cost: 0.85 gives 13 missed / 12 unnecessary, 0.9 gives 6 / 36. The seven rows the 0.9 cut rescues include a legal_or_safety case (g_053, racist album cover) and a billing case (g_023, 'pay') that no rule covers, so the guard is currently the only net under those, and it also mislabels 15 true escalations as low_confidence.

examples.reply_draft: Hey there! Can you let us know what’s happening exactly? We'll be on the lookout for your reply /AI
examples.why: Plain playback intent, correct, but 0.65 confidence on a four-word tweet sends a fine troubleshooting reply to a human.

examples.text: having trouble, cannot get the 'Browse' function to load. Only the 'Your Music' or 'search' work?!?
examples.reply_draft: Hey there! Best thing to try here is a reinstall. Just follow the steps on our help site. Let us know how you get on! /AI
examples.why: Correct intent, correct reinstall steps, shipped by the judge, escalated only because confidence was 0.85.

examples.text: When my EQ is on, my music always cracks when a song starts. Is there a fix? Thanks
examples.reply_draft: Hey there! Can you let us know what device, OS, and Spotify version you're running? We'll see what we can suggest. /AI
examples.why: Correct intent and a concrete EQ troubleshooting reply; the 0.85 confidence is about tweet vagueness, not intent.

proposed_fix: Cover the seven rescued patterns with rules (legal: 'racist|racism|offensive'; money: 'pay|paying|payment'; caption rule from fm3; DM-consistency rule from fm1), then re-run choose_threshold on dev with min_recall 0.9; expect the chosen threshold to fall to 0.85 and unnecessary escalations to drop from 36 to about 12-15 on test with recall >= 0.90. Report reason-code accuracy excluding low_confidence rows so the guard's relabelling is visible.

title: playlist_or_library boundary unchanged since v1: F1 0.50, 12 errors, 9 shared
hypothesis: Library and playlist limits phrased as demands go to feature_request_or_feedback or subscription_or_plan (g_044, g_063, g_112, g_148, g_162, g_141), and tweets where 'playlist' is only the object of a bug, plan or login problem get playlist_or_library on the noun (g_004, g_082, g_194, g_195, g_233, g_025). 9 of 12 are shared with zero-shot and 10 of 12 are identical to v1, so this is a taxonomy-description problem, not retrieval: the intents.yaml description lists 'playlist how-tos' but not limits, and playback_or_app_bug does not say 'even when the symptom is on a playlist'. Cost is moderate: 8 of the 12 were still handled correctly (auto_handle) and only g_233 is gold escalate.

examples.text: I have reached my 10,000 song limit on a playlist that I’ve been working on for years now. Is there any work around for this? If not, are there any thoughts of expanding this limit. Expanding limits are in right now. Ask Twitter #Limitless
examples.reply_draft: Hey there! We don't have any info on this right now, but we'll be sure to let the right team know it's something you'd like to see. /AI
examples.why: A 10,000-song playlist limit question is playlist_or_library by the guide; the wish to expand it pulled it to feature request.

examples.text: I need help! The app keeps creating new playlists labelled "tracks" with only one song in each one. How do I stop this?
examples.reply_draft: Hey there! Sorry to hear that. Could you let us know what device you're using and your Spotify app version? We'll take a look 🙂 /AI
examples.why: The app creating playlists is an app malfunction; 'playlists' as the object of the bug won the label and the reply asks for device details.

examples.text: Why do you limit the albums that we save, understand the limit for downloaded ones, it really seems unnecessary when thinking about the price we pay monthly
examples.reply_draft: Hey there! There's currently a 10k limit in Your Music (Songs + Albums + Artists). More info here: /AI
examples.why: Saved-albums limit is a library question; both agent and zero-shot read the complaint as a plan/price question.

proposed_fix: Edit config/intents.yaml descriptions: playlist_or_library gains 'library/playlist/download limits (10k songs, 3,333 downloads) even when phrased as a complaint'; playback_or_app_bug gains 'including bugs whose symptom is a playlist'; feature_request_or_feedback gains 'not limits that already have a documented answer'. Add these six rows' patterns to the dev set check. Test: playlist_or_library F1 >= 0.70 on test with feature_request_or_feedback precision not below 0.65.
